candidates.full: AP: Vens uticao na upravni odbor Nvidije da Huang treba opet da bude rukovodilac Potpredsednik SAD Džej-Di Vens bio je taj koji se tokom vikenda intenzivno angažovao kako bi, u ime predsednika Donalda Trampa, ubedio upravni odbor Nvidije (Nvidia) da Džensen Huang treba da se vrati na funkciju izvršnog direktora te američke kompanije koja proizvodi čipove, rekla je večeras AP-u osoba upućena u ovu situaciju. Oglas Ta osoba, koja je tražila anonimnost zbog neovlašćenosti da iznosi podatke u javnost, ukazala je da Bela kuća smatra da Vens - koji je pre ulaska u politiku radio u Silicijumskoj dolini - poseduje neophodan autoritet da deluje kao efikasan posrednik. Kako je navedeno, njegovo posredništvo sastojalo se u tome da se članovima upravnog odbora Nvidije pomogne da prevaziđu rezerve u pogledu ponovnog postavljanja Huanga na funkciju izvršnog direktora. To ponovno postavljanje dogodilo se danas, iznenadivši javnost, a učinjeno je, po svoj prilici, na podsticaj predsednika Trampa. Samo nekoliko dana ranije, upravni odbor je odbio Huangovu ponudu da se vrati na čelo kompanije, odakle je delovao kao jedan od ključnih svetskih zagovarača veštačke inteligencije. Iznenadna promena mišljenja najnoviji je obrt u drami koja je nastala kada je Huang priznao da je varao suprugu ni manje ni više nego sa ženom koja je osumnjičena da špijunira za Kinu. Pročitajte još: Tramp, koji ima blizak lični odnos sa Huangu, tražio je njegovo vraćanje na funkciju najkasnije u nedelju uveče i sebi je danas propisao zaslugu za odluku upravnog odbora Nvidije. "Verujem da je moja intervencija bila vrlo važna", rekao je Tramp za televiziju Es-En-Bi-Si (CNBC) i preneo da je upravnom odboru Nvidije dao uveravanja da Huang ne predstavlja pretnju po nacionalnu bezbednost SAD. Takođe nije želeo da kaže da li se daljinski uključio u radi upravnog odbora, ali je izjavio: "U osnovi, bio sam zastupljen na upravnom odboru". Nvidija igra krucijalnu ulogu u industriji veštačke inteligencije i dominira tržištem kompjuterskih čipova koji se koriste za obuku i pokretanje AI modela. Ima i mnoga partnerstva i investicije u kompanijama koje proizvode čipove. Huangov povratak ne donosi sam po sebi njegovo oslobađanje od odgovornosti, jer ga očekuje nekoliko kongresnih istraga zbog implikacija Huangovog skandala po nacionalnu bezbednost SAD. candidates.summary: Компания Nvidia и ее бывший гендиректор Дженсен Хуанг могут попасть под уголовное преследование в Калифорнии, заявил генпрокурор американского штата Роб Бонта агентству Bloomberg. Причины. Калифорнийская прокуратура начала расследование в отношении компании и ее бывшего главы, сейчас оно находится н
candidates.full: Компания Nvidia и ее бывший гендиректор Дженсен Хуанг могут попасть под уголовное преследование в Калифорнии, заявил генпрокурор американского штата Роб Бонта агентству Bloomberg. Причины. Калифорнийская прокуратура начала расследование в отношении компании и ее бывшего главы, сейчас оно находится на начальном этапе, рассказал Бонта. По его словам, ведомство направило Nvidia повестку с требованием предоставить информацию. На сайте Минюста Калифорнии говорится, что генпрокурор штата запросил у компании данные о том, могли ли ее передовые чипы или конфиденциальная информация попасть в Китай, а также вводила ли Nvidia инвесторов и общественность в заблуждение. Если выяснится, что Nvidia и Хуанг сознательно обманывали инвесторов и общество по поводу продаж передовых чипов Китаю, это может стать причиной для уголовного преследования, пояснил генпрокурор Калифорнии. «Основной правовой базой, на которую мы опираемся, являются предусмотренные законодательством Калифорнии запреты — в рамках как гражданского, так и уголовного права — на введение инвесторов и общественности в заблуждение», — сказал Бонта. Новая газета. Европа — Читайте также Если расследование придет к выводу, что Nvidia и Хуанг нарушили закон, от компании могут потребовать вернуть прибыль от незаконных продаж, отметил генпрокурор. Он добавил, что уголовное преследование также может привести к штрафам. Другие расследования. Президент США Дональд Трамп заявил, что ФБР расследует связи Хуанга с бывшей главой сингапурской компании Megaspeed Элис Хуанг, которую подозревают в сотрудничестве с китайской разведкой. Министр финансов США Скотт Бессент отметил, что собственное расследование Nvidia поможет установить, допустила ли компания «безответственный» подход к продаже передовых микросхем, из-за чего они могли оказаться в Китае. Скандал с главой Nvidia. 12 ноября Дженсен Хуанг ушел с поста гендиректора компании и покинул совет директоров на фоне сообщений о его отношениях с Элис Хуанг. За женщиной наблюдали спецслужбы США и, как утверждают источники NYT, пришли к выводу, что она передавала информацию Пекину. Затем они обнаружили ее близкие отношения с Хуангом. Пекин отрицает, что Элис Хуанг была шпионкой. Генпрокурор США Тодд Бланш 12 ноября заявил, что Министерство юстиции еще не пришло к выводу, связана ли она со спецслужбами КНР.

candidates.title: ONU va stabili reguli privind folosirea în luptă a „roboților ucigași". Care este principalul dezacord între statele membre
candidates.summary: ONU va stabili reguli privind folosirea în luptă a „roboților ucigași”. Care este principalul dezacord între statele membre Cele 128 de state părţi la Convenţia ONU privind anumite arme convenţionale au ajuns, sâmbătă, la un compromis pentru continuarea procesului de reglementare a armelor autonome
candidates.full: ONU va stabili reguli privind folosirea în luptă a „roboților ucigași”. Care este principalul dezacord între statele membre Cele 128 de state părţi la Convenţia ONU privind anumite arme convenţionale au ajuns, sâmbătă, la un compromis pentru continuarea procesului de reglementare a armelor autonome letale, cunoscute şi sub denumirea de „roboţi ucigaşi”, după o săptămână de negocieri dificile la Geneva. Acordul prevede elaborarea unui instrument internaţional în următorii doi ani, fără a stabili deocamdată ce formă va avea acesta. Toate cele 128 de state au acceptat lansarea procesului, inclusiv cele cinci puteri nucleare membre permanente ale Consiliului de Securitate al ONU: Statele Unite, Rusia, China, Franţa şi Regatul Unit, relatează EFE, citată de Agerpres. Compromisul nu prevede interzicerea armelor autonome letale şi nici nu stabileşte dacă viitorul acord va avea caracter obligatoriu sau voluntar. Aceste chestiuni vor trebui clarificate în cadrul discuţiilor viitoare, după cum a explicat preşedintele conferinţei, ambasadorul elveţian Julien Thoeni. El a arătat că statele vor trebui să stabilească şi ce categorii de arme ar putea fi interzise în baza dreptului internaţional umanitar şi care ar putea fi reglementate. Statele care se opun caracterului obligatoriu al convenției Unele delegaţii s-au opus folosirii termenului „negociere”, iar în textul final acesta a fost înlocuit cu „elaborare”, potrivit AFP. Formularea lasă deschisă posibilitatea ca viitorul instrument internaţional să aibă caracter obligatoriu sau voluntar. Aproximativ 100 de state au susţinut adoptarea unor reguli obligatorii din punct de vedere juridic pentru armele autonome letale, în timp ce Statele Unite, Rusia şi Israelul s-au opus unei astfel de propuneri, potrivit Reuters şi Kyodo. Unul dintre obstacolele principale a fost opoziţia unor state, în special a Rusiei. Potrivit Reuters, AFP şi DPA, Moscova s-a opus încă de la început adoptării agendei conferinţei şi participării unor observatori, printre care şi Uniunea Europeană. Deciziile în cadrul Convenţiei se iau prin consensul celor 128 de state membre, iar opoziţia unei singure ţări poate bloca un acord, consemnează dpa. Brazilia şi alte state au susţinut necesitatea unor reguli internaţionale într-un termen cât mai scurt. Ambasadorul brazilian Frederico Meyer a rezumat diferenţele dintre cele două tabere, spunând, potrivit AFP, că unele ţări dispun de putere, în timp ce altele au majoritatea de partea lor. Compromisul a fost prezentat de preşedintele conferinţei, Julien Thoeni, drept un rezultat important după mai bine de un deceniu de discuţii. Reuters relatează că diplomatul a descris înţelegerea drept o realizare semnificativă pentru dezarmarea umanitară, în timp ce reprezentanţii organizaţiilor neguvernamentale au avut o evaluare mult mai rezervată. Riscurile armelor ghidate de AI pentru populația civilă Coaliţia Stop Killer Robots, care reuneşte peste 300 de organizaţii, a criticat decizia adoptată, apreciind că aceasta nu oferă o direcţie clară către un instrument obligatoriu juridic. Nicole van Rooijen, directoarea executivă a coaliţiei, a avertizat, într-o declaraţie citată de Reuters şi AFP, că amânarea creării unui instrument obligatoriu juridic pune în pericol civilii şi umanitatea. La rândul său, Verity Coyle, directoare adjunctă a programului pentru arme al Human Rights Watch, a considerat, potrivit AFP, că rezultatul nu oferă măsurile urgente necesare, în condiţiile în care tehnologia avansează rapid. Miza reglementării este legată de capacitatea acestor sisteme de a identifica şi ataca ţinte fără intervenţie umană în procesul decizional. EFE explică faptul că armele autonome letale nu se limitează la drone, ci pot lua forma unor tancuri, submarine sau sisteme de apărare antiaeriană şi antirachetă, funcţionarea lor bazându-se pe algoritmi şi inteligenţă artificială. Potrivit Reuters, îngrijorările privind utilizarea acestor tehnologii au crescut pe fondul conflictelor din Ucraina, Sudan şi Orientul Mijlociu. Comitetul Internaţional al Crucii Roşii susţine interzicerea armelor autonome cu funcţionare imprevizibilă, precum şi a celor care vizează oameni, precizează AFP. Organizaţia consideră că dezvoltarea acestor sisteme ridică probleme privind protecţia civililor, responsabilitatea pentru atacuri şi respectarea dreptului internaţional umanitar. Şefa ONU pentru dezarmare, Izumi Nakamitsu, a declarat, potrivit Kyodo şi Reuters, că urmează o perioadă de negocieri intense, într-un interval de timp foarte scurt. Până în 2028, statele vor trebui să stabilească forma viitorului instrument internaţional şi dacă prevederile acestuia vor avea caracter obligatoriu sau voluntar.

candidates.full: Yritys sopia autonomisten tappavien asejärjestelmien sääntelystä ei tuottanut tulosta Genevessä pidetyssä YK-kokouksessa. Lauantaiaamun pikkutunneilla päättyneessä kokouksessa 128 osanottajamaata päätyivät muotoilemaan pelisääntöjä kahden tulevan vuoden aikana. Kansalaisjärjestöt olivat tulokseen pettyneitä, koska ne olivat tavoitelleet laillisesti sitovia rajoja. Useimmat jäsenmaat kannattivat sääntöjen kirjaamista, mutta teknologiaa jo kehittäneet maat eivät olleet halukkaita asettamaan sille rajoituksia. Tähän ryhmään kuuluvat muun muassa Yhdysvallat ja Venäjä. Yli 300:n kansalaisjärjestön muodostama Stop Killer Robots -koalitio huomautti, että itsenäisiä asejärjestelmiä on jo nyt käytössä muun muassa Ukrainan sodassa. YK:n aseriisuntapäällikkö Izumi Nakamitsu kehotti YK:n jäsenmaita tarttumaan ripeästi toimeen, jotta säännöistä saataisiin mahdollisimman sitovat.

candidates.full: Within a few hours of each other (timeline), two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics (Scientific American). Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code (1.3GB worth, ~250,000 page equivalent) rather than a full paper. Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is GRH and puts the chance of a Lean bug well under 1%. So if it finishes compiling with no extra axioms, it is probably correct, and no human will ever have read all of it… …prompting Alessandro Masullo to release his 940 page, 100% human, work in progress proof he had been working on for the last 12 years (and had been undergoing secret manual review and revision per Kevin Hartnett). This is the third in the trilogy of frontier math breakthroughs, following from the Navier Stokes solutions and the Quasi-Riemann bounding, but it doesn’t feel over. OpenAI's September Navier-Stokes claim is still the cautionary tale: critics argued that its Lean proof did not match the natural-language result. Both AI-claimed Millennium Prize results will take years to verify. Apart from the incredible accomplishment of the most famous problem in mathematics, one cannot miss the contrast that the AI-written solution is probably correct but incomprehensible, and the other solution is probably technically incorrect but understandable. Sponsored by Agentfield.AI Open models are ready. Most coding harnesses aren’t. On DeepSWE, CodeAF finished #1 of ten on the same open model, ahead of Claude Code, at the lowest cost per fix. As Levent eloquently put it: “Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” This also ties into other AI themes we’ve covered on the podcast and on this newsletter: The nature of Slop: Levent says “I am presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics. It being obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of "slop", I decided to only present Lean.” One of the key tenets of the No Slop Manifesto is that you should understand what you ship (“Slop is when we put less effort into producing something than we ask the consumer to spend understanding it.”). And yet, this giant pile of Lean is verifiably correct and is incredibly significant in human history. Should we have delayed its release by a decade simply because we didn’t understand every single bit of it? Weak to Strong alignment: the typical experience of using agents is Strong to Weak - we are general intelligences guiding not-as-smart AI to do things we know how to do well. We also often expect AI to automate most work “within distribution”, and expect it to run into more trouble at the limits of capability where the “centaur” pattern of human-AI-collaboration is required. Levent’s lived experience is the opposite - collaborating with Claude only in the early stages and then leaving him far behind with the critical parts involving automorphic forms on higher-rank groups. We are starting to need Weak to Strong alignment — the open ended domain of controlling AI smarter than us. Sponsored by Backblaze B2 If your data is growing faster than planned, you need storage that grows with your business, feeds flash and GPUs with terabit-scale throughput, and doesn’t charge egress. Backblaze B2 has delivered capacity tier storage for twenty years, manages more than six exabytes, and is trusted by leading neoclouds, labs, and gen AI companies. Growth shouldn’t be something you sweat. We’ve got room for whatever you’re building. Claimed Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude The claim: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says that, "working with Claude," he has found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. He says the method also covers the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) (Scientific American, statement summary, remark.pdf link). Artifact: Only Lean code was released. A written-out prose version reportedly ran past 250,000 pages (timeline). Timeline: The work began on Oct 6. Eight of the 20 steps landed on Nov 15, and the final entry on Nov 16 reads "GRH." Alpöge credits Claude for the parts involving automorphic forms on higher-rank groups, an area where he says he has little mastery (breakdown). Unknowns: The Claude model used and the degree of human steering have not been disclosed (open questions). Verification status: Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is GRH. The Lean code is "still compiling, will take a few hours." He puts the chance of a Lean bug at <<1% (analysis). Provisional status: Artificial Analysis notes that both AI-claimed Millennium results are unverified: this one and OpenAI's September Navier-Stokes claim, which used an unreleased model (tally). Competing human proof: Alessandro Masullo has announced a separate, purely human proof of RH. It is reported as a roughly 940-page GRH draft (announcement, page count). Interpretation debate: Some argue the result shows we have little idea how hard math problems objectively are, rather than showing broad superhuman ability (Theo Jaffee, Ege Erdil). Brute-force framing: Others compare the approach to olympiad-style "bashing" at a scale humans lack the willpower for (cloneofsimo). Jaggedness: Omar Khattab notes the contrast between solving Millennium problems and being "this dumb on 1000 other things" (post). Market reaction: ANT stock fell about 10% on the day (scaling01, Nabeel Qureshi). Unconfirmed rumor: A DeepMind "math horizon" repo appearing the same day prompted speculation about Gemini math results (unconfirmed). Thinking Machines Releases Inkling 2 Mini, an Open-Weights Looped Transformer Inkling 2 Mini: A 26.4B-parameter looped MoE under Apache 2.0, pitched as small enough for a laptop. It scores 20.1 on the AA Index (launch, Mira Murati). Architecture: There are 12 shared core layers run for 3 passes, with gated messages carried between passes (vLLM). Active parameters: 3.4B unique active parameters, or 5.4B effective counting the loops. It has a 1M context window and accepts text and image input (AA). Training recipe: Two-thirds of the experts were pruned during mid-training, followed by logit distillation from a larger Inkling (eliebakouch). Claimed results: It leads open models under 100B on DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%) (via teortaxes). Comparison to Inkling 1.0: It reportedly beats Inkling 1.0 at 2.7% of the size (Ziqiao Ma). Independent evals: Vals: It ties Claude Opus 5.5 on CyberBench at under a quarter of the cost and keeps 96–97% of Inkling 2 Small's Vibe Code and SAGE scores (Vals, details). Artificial Analysis: AA places it on the Pareto frontier for intelligence vs. active parameters (AA). ARC-AGI-2: It reportedly scores 49.3% at $0.14/task, well below Inkling 2 Small (teortaxes). Safety and interpretability rationale: Thinking Machines says the open release is meant to let researchers study how loops affect chain-of-thought monitorability (Alex Robey). Variable-loop model: A companion research model, TML-d24-varloop-research, shows long-context scores (GraphWalks, MRCR v2) improving with more passes. Knowledge benchmarks such as SimpleQA and AA-Omniscience do not improve (Ziqiao Ma). Goodfire analysis: Goodfire mapped information flow across layers, blocks and loops (Goodfire). NDIF hosting: NDIF hosts both models with tooling for activation patching across loops (NDIF). Serving and local availability: vLLM had day-0 support. GB200 decode: TP1 decode on GB200 drops from 10.29 to 3.84 ms at batch 1, with kernels per step falling from 4,278 to 927 (numbers). Local runtimes: Ollama 0.40.17-rc3 (Ollama), Unsloth GGUF quants targeting 16GB RAM (Unsloth), transformers, llama.cpp and MLX (HF). Hands-on reports: Soumith Chintala reports about 75 tok/s decode on a DGX Spark and evals "roughly as good as Qwen 3.8 27B" (post). Gemini 4 Neon: Developer Reception, Evals and Access Developer reception: Strong practitioner praise for Neon's usability (Theo, systematicls). Lucas Beyer comparison: In a side-by-side against Opus 5.5, Muse Wonder Full and Sol 6.2, all four models built a working dataset viewer. Neon's was the most data-aware (Lucas Beyer). Cyber evals: Thoughtful Lab says Neon found subtle vulnerabilities other models missed while using a fraction of the tokens (Karina Nguyen). Benchmarks: Company Agent Bench: 87.4%, ahead of Fable 5.2 (82.2%) and GPT-6.2 Astra (79.7%) (results). Agent Arena Index: Debuted at #2 with 1336 points (Arena). FutureSim: Highest score, using 500+ subagents (post). FrontierCode 2.0: 46.2% vs. Opus 5.5's 47.3%, at roughly a third of the cost ($4.38 vs. $12.82 per task) (roundup). Pricing and access concerns: One tester paid $4.60 for 15M tokens on a simple demo and called it non-competitive against Anthropic's subscription limits (teortaxes). Antigravity terms: Developers raised concerns about account bans and headless-use rules in Antigravity (linaqruf). Third-party harnesses (attributed): Gemini subscriptions will reportedly work in any harness starting Dec 2 (kimmonismus). Naming confusion: Users are unsure how Neon, Carbon, Argon and Hydrogen relate (Simon Willison). Gemini 4 Hydrogen: The speed-focused model is live in the Gemini app and Search (Google). API additions: Dynamic Tool Retrieval: Supports deferred functions and remote MCP servers with server-side tool search (Phil Schmid). Gemini 3.5 Transcribe: Voice editing is now in public preview in the Gemini API (Google). GIF generation: Available in the Gemini app, powered by Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash (Gemini App). Evals, Alignment and Measurement METR research update: METR says AI R&D-relevant capabilities are improving rapidly and are getting harder to measure (METR, post). Time Horizons 2.0: Doubling time is 3.6 months. GPT-6 Astra reaches 40.3h and Opus 5.5 39.0h, with a 95% CI spanning about 11.9 hours to 110 days (scaling01). Verifiability gap: Horizons are much longer on easy-to-verify tasks than on hard-to-verify ones (plots). METR Capability Index (MCI): Its trends track Epoch's ECI closely (Rowan Huang). Swarms: Larger agent swarms showed "echo-chamber" overfitting to their self-generated tests (appendix). Human baselines: Only roughly world-class experts still beat models on verifiable tasks (Tenobrus). Reward hacking: Recent OpenAI models reward-hack most often on the new suite (data). Arena indexes: OpenAI holds the top seven spots on the updated Alignment Index, with Claude Fable 5.2 at #8 (Arena). Misalignment tracking and judge behavior: Vals launched a public Misalignment Incidents page for cheating and reward hacking (Vals). Hyperstition judge-time scaling: Models act as token-level "editor judges" for RL. Fable 5.2 closed 68% of the Qwen2.5-7B base-to-Instruct gap on MATH using about 1% of standard GRPO tokens (thread). Observed failures: Neon hallucinated tool results and a nonexistent checkpoint. Astra leaked its scratchpad into replies. Domain benchmarks: Hospital-bench: GPT-6.2 Astra leads with a 62.4% mean score, while Opus 5.5 fully passed the most tasks (17/48). Disclosure of restricted patient records was a common harm (summary). AA-Robotics v0.1: Astra used the fewest arm commands of any model tested (AA). OpenAI MedChemBench: A new benchmark for medicinal chemistry reasoning (OpenAI). AA Search Index: Parallel Search scores 83, tied for top. Its fast mode costs about $0.014 per task (AA). Agent memory and research agents: Weight-space abliteration: Outer models read and edited Qwen3.5-0.8B weights directly. Zero-shot, Opus 5.5 cut refusal from 0.80 to 0.55; with 10 forward passes, runs rediscovered the Arditi et al. recipe, reaching about 0.17–0.21 (Varun Gangal). Other research: Counterfactual JEPAs: Raise counterfactual R² from 38–46% to 86–96% (alphaXiv). SMELT looped MoE: Saves 6.8–18% of training FLOPs (post). DiLoCo on MaxText: Uses 65x less bandwidth (Arthur Douillard). Stripe fraud distillation: An explanation-distillation recipe gives 39% higher recall (Emily Sands). Small ARC model: A 19M-parameter model scores 70% on ARC-1 (post). Other Model Launches Tencent Hy4: Open weights for a 770B/49B-active natively multimodal MoE with 1M context, released with a system card (Tencent). Serving: Day-0 vLLM support covers BF16 and FP8 (vLLM). Safety evaluation: Neel Nanda praised the third-party loss-of-control evaluation (Neel Nanda). Microsoft Ignite: Announcements include MAI Code 2, claimed at 96% of Opus 5.5's performance for 5% of the cost, plus the Autopilot agent and the Decision-1.1 router (recap). Additional releases: Industry and Policy Anthropic IPO: Described as the largest IPO ever, raising $81.3B at pricing and $93.5B including the underwriters' option, at $83 a share (numbers). Isomorphic Labs: Raised a $5B Series C (same source). US–China: Trump said he and Xi agreed to "joint guardrails" on AI, with no details given (video quote). Chip manufacturing rules: New US rules may block TSMC and Samsung from manufacturing Chinese AI chips (Kyle Chan). Nscale and ByteDance: Nscale needs a license to give ByteDance remote GPU access; ByteDance made up about 73% of its 2025 revenue (Techmeme). Malaysia smuggling estimate: Epoch finds trade records consistent with more than $3B of smuggled servers, roughly 150k H100-equivalents (Epoch). Nvidia leadership: Following Jensen Huang's resignation, Trump urged Nvidia to reinstate him (report). OpenAI distillation research: OpenAI published work on detecting and disrupting distillation attacks on its models (OpenAI). candidates.full: Австралійський ентузіаст Майкл зібрав домашню систему для локального запуску моделей штучного інтелекту, під’єднавши чотири вживані графічні прискорювачі Nvidia Tesla V100 із 32 ГБ відеопам’яті кожен до міні-ПК Lenovo ThinkCentre M720q Tiny. Сукупний обсяг відеопам’яті установки становить 128 ГБ, а її вартість автор оцінив приблизно у 3500 доларів США без урахування місцевих податків. За даними BBC News, міні-ПК оснащено процесором Intel Core i5-9400T та 64 ГБ оперативної пам’яті DDR4. Відеокарти з’єднані через PCIe-перемикач CEACENT CNOL4PE08 і чотири кабелі OCuLink. Кожна Tesla V100 працює через інтерфейс PCIe Gen3 x4. Стандартна прошивка Lenovo обмежувала конфігурацію двома графічними картами. За описом автора, BIOS виділяв для 64-бітних пристроїв вікно обсягом 128 ГБ, тоді як для кожної V100 із 32 ГБ пам’яті потрібно 64 ГБ адресного простору. Після підключення третьої карти система зупинялася на етапі POST. Для обходу цього обмеження Майкл використав coreboot 26.09 з корисним навантаженням EDK2 та увімкнув розподіл пам’яті above-4G. Це збільшило доступне вікно приблизно до 486 ГБ. Додатково він модифікував райзер: PCIe-перемикач не активував контакт присутності, потрібний для подачі живлення на слот. Прошивання BIOS виконували програматором CH341A із затискачем SOIC8. Для кожної карти використано зовнішню док-станцію AOOSTAR AG01 із вбудованим блоком живлення на 800 Вт. Пасивно охолоджувані Tesla V100 отримали надруковані на 3D-принтері повітропроводи з 140-міліметровими вентиляторами Noctua. Окремий вентилятор охолоджує PCIe-перемикач усередині міні-ПК. Рівень шуму готової системи автор виміряв на позначці близько 62 дБ з відстані один метр. Кожну V100 обмежено споживанням на рівні 200 Вт, тобто до 800 Вт для чотирьох карт. Скрипт контролює температуру найгарячішого прискорювача: він зупиняє обчислення за 83 °C та вимикає систему за 87 °C. У тесті Qwen3.8-27B Q6 одна карта обробляла приблизно 40 токенів за секунду, а чотири карти — близько 285 токенів за секунду за одночасної роботи з чотирма запитами.

candidates.summary: ADELPHI, Md. – The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command, known as DEVCOM, Army Research Laboratory recently executed several partnership agreements with industry collaborators working in additive manufacturing, sensing and energy technologies to accelerate the transition of scientific i
candidates.full: ADELPHI, Md. – The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command, known as DEVCOM, Army Research Laboratory recently executed several partnership agreements with industry collaborators working in additive manufacturing, sensing and energy technologies to accelerate the transition of scientific innovation toward military application. Partnerships with Trusted Metal LLC, OmniSpectra Inc. and Bethlehem Steel Corp. illustrate how ARL pairs its fundamental research with collaboration tools to promote the growth of the defense industrial base. ARL holds the largest portfolio of active patents in the Army — the result of more than three decades of translating its scientific discoveries into frameworks for innovative solutions. ARL’s arsenal of partnership mechanisms, meanwhile, ensure that the laboratory’s patented research reaches the hands of capable industry partners and, ultimately, the warfighter. “We have a wide breadth of expertise at ARL on both the science side and the business side that we can leverage to solve the Army’s scientific and technological problems,” said Wendy Leonard, chief of ARL’s Acquisition Management and Technology Transfer Branch. “ARL’s fundamental research often sets the scientific foundation for new capabilities that don’t yet exist in the commercial sector. By executing new partnership agreements, we expand not only the Army’s network of industry partners but also the nation’s economic base.” Access to a diverse set of partnership mechanisms grants ARL researchers the flexibility to tailor their collaboration approach to fit the needs of both small businesses and industry leaders, while also lowering the barriers to industry participation at all stages of the defense innovation process. The following examples of recent Army-industry engagements highlight a few of the partnership mechanisms that ARL regularly employs to help align U.S. business interest with Army goals and advance the transition of warfighter-focused innovations. Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) ARL employs CRADAs to formalize collaborative partnerships with outside parties which allows the exchange of ideas and shared resources for a mutually beneficial objective. Each party is responsible for the costs of their contribution to the joint project. ARL executed a CRADA with Trusted Metal, LLC to determine the best technology specifications for a laser powder bed fusion system, a popular additive manufacturing tool widely used by companies for 3D-printing metal components. Because industry does not yet have a universally accepted standard for how an LPBF machine should be built, the structural properties of LPBF-based 3D prints can vary widely, forcing the Army to spend months on quality control testing. ARL researchers will collaborate with Trusted Metal, a startup with proprietary technology for enforcing LPBF-based print standards, to create a solution that will ensure consistent print quality. Commercial Evaluation License (CEL) ARL employs CELs to provide companies interested in an ARL invention the opportunity to evaluate and explore the invention’s commercial viability. ARL executed a CEL with OmniSpectra, Inc. that allows the company to evaluate ARL’s patented high-voltage sensor technology. This sensor, unlike existing commercial variants, does not dissipate excessive power and can account for interference from electromagnetic fields and temperature variations to provide more accurate readings. The invention, which can sense voltages up to 30 kilovolts while dissipating less than one watt of power, supports Army efforts to advance the development of technologies relevant to pulsed power and directed energy. At the end of its one-year evaluation period, OmniSpectra will submit a final report to ARL summarizing the results of its evaluation and receive the option to apply for a patent license. Patent Licensing Agreement (PLA) ARL employs PLAs to establish the terms and conditions under which a company can make, sell or use a patented ARL invention for the purposes of commercialization. Access to ARL intellectual property in this manner enables licensees to capitalize on ARL’s scientific innovations to develop new technologies for commercial sales that the Army can also leverage on the battlefield in the future. ARL executed a PLA with Bethlehem Steel Corporation that negotiated the licensing of its patented aluminum-based nanogalvanic powder that rapidly produces hydrogen gas when it comes in contact with any liquid containing water. This invention could inform future portable and expeditionary energy solutions for the Army, providing a compact means to generate hydrogen when and where needed. The agreement with Bethlehem Steel marks the fourth PLA, in addition to an existing CEL, that ARL executed for this patent, demonstrating the invention’s application potential as an easily transportable on-demand energy source with high volumetric energy density. ABOUT DEVCOM ARL DEVCOM ARL is the Army’s sole fundamental research laboratory serving as the nexus of science between the military, academia and industry. Operating under the U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command, ARL executes globally recognized research to accelerate delivery of war-winning, disruptive technologies for tomorrow’s Army. candidates.full: Про це розповів в інтерв'ю «Шелтеру» голова Наглядової ради Brave1 Олександр Борняков. За його словами, понад 774 тисячі дронів та іншої техніки на $1,15 мільярда вже поставлено. Тобто близько 86% замовлених одиниць уже на фронті, решта — у виробництві та логістиці. Борняков зазначив, що те, що є у виробника в наявності, доставляють у середньому за сім днів, довше чекають нові моделі та дрони під індивідуальне завдання підрозділу, а також вироби з імпортними комплектуючими. Найвужче місце — компоненти: батареї, магніти, текстоліт для плат досі майже повністю імпортні. Затримується партія комплектуючих — затримується й дрон. Тому локалізація компонентів — один із пріоритетів Наглядової ради. Олександр Борняков Він додав, що кожна батарея в дроні є імпортною. Магніти для електродвигунів — імпортні. Текстоліт для друкованих плат — стовідсотковий імпорт. Додам тепловізійні сенсори, вуглецеві матеріали, ракетне паливо і головки самонаведення. Кристали для головок самонаведення зенітних ракет Україна востаннє виробляла у 2008 році, а цією технологією сьогодні володіють лише вісім країн. Тому Brave1 переорієнтовує підтримку на компонентну базу: вибухові й ініціювальні речовини, батареї, магніти, текстоліт, сенсори. Майже мільярд гривень уже спрямовано на масштабування виробництва вибухівки, а скоро буде грантовий конкурс на розвиток виробництва турбореактивних двигунів. Олександр Борняков Нагадаємо, Олександр Борняков в інтерв'ю "Шелтеру" також зазначив, що Україна працює над диверсифікацією супутникового зв’язку та створенням власних захищених комунікаційних рішень для військових.

candidates.title: The wind and the song: the treachery of AI
candidates.summary: From finding human figures in the stars to creating prehistoric cave art, we’ve been anthropomorphising our world for millennia. Now, machine-learning technologies can generate photorealistic images, synthetic voices that laugh and pause for breath, and chatbots that crush the Turing test. We’re see
candidates.full: From finding human figures in the stars to creating prehistoric cave art, we’ve been anthropomorphising our world for millennia. Now, machine-learning technologies can generate photorealistic images, synthetic voices that laugh and pause for breath, and chatbots that crush the Turing test. We’re seeing the first generation in history for whom the line between humans and their representations could all but vanish. In this video essay for the digital publication Fully Human, the UK animator and filmmaker Lewis Heriz interrogates where this is taking us. We inevitably build our world through symbols, he says, but the hall-of-mirrors reality we’re rapidly creating may be leading us down a perilous path. However, he argues, we’re not without agency. Instead of submitting to a world where data and people are indistinguishable, we should be thinking critically and imaginatively about how we might use AI in ways that preserve our humanity.

candidates.full: Власти РФ хотят ввести прокатные удостоверения для видеоигр по аналогии с фильмами. Разработчиков могут обязать хранить личные данные игроков, которые получит РКН. Как сообщает «Ъ», такие меры обсуждаются в правительстве в рамках доработки законопроекта «О деятельности по разработке и распространению видеоигр на территории РФ». По данным издания, власти считают необходимым выдавать играм специальные прокатные удостоверения — без них распространение проектов будет невозможным. Создателей и распространителей видеоигр могут также обязать регистрироваться в реестре организаторов распространения информации (ОРИ) Роскомнадзора. Это предполагает хранение данных на территории России и внедрение системы оперативно-разыскных мероприятий (СОРМ). Представители отрасли отмечают необходимость «равноприменимости» таких требований между российскими и иностранными разработчиками. Законопроект представили в конце 2024 года. Изначально он предусматривал, что пользователи должны будут авторизоваться в играх по номеру телефона, через «Госуслуги» или Единую биометрическую систему. Сейчас эти требования могут убрать из документа. Вопросы маркировки игрового контента будут прорабатывать дополнительно. Госдума рассчитывает принять законопроект в первом чтении до конца 2026 года. При этом глава Организации развития видеоигровой индустрии Василий Овчинников заявил «Ъ», что механизм прокатных удостоверений не подходит для игр, так как они постоянно меняются. Удостоверение, выданное при выходе игры, уже через месяц может не соответствовать ее актуальной версии. По его мнению, проверка каждой версии игры приведет к увеличению сроков согласования и дополнительным расходам. Представители отрасли также опасаются, что иностранным компаниям, особенно из «недружественных стран», будет сложно получать такие удостоверения.

candidates.title: Forget searching for GIFs, Gemini can now make its own
candidates.summary: Google Gemini can now make GIFs, meaning there’s one less reason to scroll endlessly through GIF libraries looking for the perfect reaction. The feature lets users generate short animated loops using text prompts, photos, or videos. ChatGPT can already create GIFs of its own, and Google is now joini
candidates.full: Google Gemini can now make GIFs, meaning there’s one less reason to scroll endlessly through GIF libraries looking for the perfect reaction. The feature lets users generate short animated loops using text prompts, photos, or videos. ChatGPT can already create GIFs of its own, and Google is now joining the party with its Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video model. Gemini can turn prompts into looping GIFs Users can simply describe the animation they want in Gemini’s main chat, or open the image and video creation tools, select GIF from the format picker, and enter a prompt. There are also ready-made templates for creating reaction memes, while uploaded photos and videos can serve as references for more personalised results. The generated animations run for approximately three seconds and loop automatically. Once ready, they can be copied and pasted into supported apps, messages, emails, and documents, or downloaded directly as standard .gif files. Free for some, paid for others GIF generation is rolling out to Google AI subscribers globally, while free users can access it in eight countries: the US, Canada, UK, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Germany, and France. The rollout is gradual, so even eligible users may not see the feature immediately. Gemini’s help documentation currently still lists a Google AI plan as a requirement, despite Google’s announcement that free access is available in those markets. It’s a neat addition, especially for anyone who would rather create a custom reaction than settle for the same tired GIF everyone has been sharing for years. With Google and OpenAI now offering similar tools, AI-generated GIFs could become another everyday chatbot feature. Whether the results are actually meme-worthy is a different question. В официално изявление от комисията посоч
candidates.full: Комисията по банково дело, жилищно строителство и градски въпроси към Сената на САЩ обяви, че Дженсън Хуан – изпълнителният директор и президент на Nvidia, който днес бе възстановен на поста си, ще даде показания пред комисията на 3 декември, предаде Ройтерс. В официално изявление от комисията посочват, че изслушването, озаглавено "Защита на предимството на Америка в сферата на изкуствения интелект: Надзор върху американския експортен контрол", ще бъде открито заседание в хибриден формат. Това означава, че част от участниците ще присъстват лично, а други ще се включат чрез видеовръзка. Изслушването се провежда след като Хуан временно се оттегли от длъжността си заради връзка с предполагаема китайска шпионка – ситуация, която породи опасения относно националната сигурност на САЩ и износа на чувствителни технологии за Китай. Междувременно редица американски законодатели и от двете партии отправиха остри критики към решението на Nvidia да върне Дженсън Хуан на поста главен изпълнителен директор. Те заявиха, че Конгресът трябва да приеме законодателство, което да ограничи износа на американски чипове за Китай, и настояха за отговори по случая. Демократът Елизабет Уорън, сенатор от Масачузетс, която от януари ще оглави Комисията по банкови въпроси, определи решението за връщането на Хуан като "безразсъдно". Тя добави, че бордът на директорите все още дължи на Конгреса отговори относно това дали компанията спазва американските правила за контрол на износа. "Завръщането на Дженсън Хуан прави още по-належащо приемането на двупартийни законопроекти за контрол на износа. Трябва да гарантираме, че Nvidia няма да лобира за провалянето на тези закони, което би изложило на риск националната ни сигурност", заяви Уорън. Преди нея лидерът на демократите в Сената Чък Шумър заяви, че връщането на Хуан на поста показва колко е важно да се приеме законодателство за затягане на ограниченията върху износа на американски чипове за Китай. Републиканецът Дон Бейкън, конгресмен от Небраска, коментира: "Хуан е бил компрометиран и използван от китайски шпионин. Nvidia трябваше да продължи напред без него и да игнорира необяснимото желание на администрацията да го спаси. Конгресът трябва да разбере кой точно е одобрил продажбите на високотехнологични компютърни чипове за Китай". Републиканският сенатор от Тексас - Джон Корнин също постави под въпрос решението на борда на Nvidia. "Няма риск за националната сигурност? На какво основание?", написа Корнин в платформата "X". Републиканският сенатор Джон Къртис заяви, че иска разяснения относно възстановяването на длъжност. "Кой от правителството ни е изразил становище? Какво са казали на управляващия борд на Nvidia? И въз основа на какво бордът е стигнал до заключението, че няма риск. Миналата седмица бордът заяви, че не възнамерява да го връща на поста. Бих искал да знам какво се е променило", посочи Къртис.

candidates.full: Regularity is not the same as consistency Since we are talking about the Lviv aircraft factory, we can recall that one of the most popular reasons for criticizing the organization of fire damage is that the target is hit once, called destroyed and no longer remembered. So, the example of the aircraft factory in Lviv shows that this has not been so relevant for a couple of years. The facility was first hit back in March 2022, and the total number of attacks has probably exceeded a dozen. It got to the point that the company didn't even spare the same "Hazel". And this is not an isolated example. It may be recalled that the Ukrainian energy sector has been hit since October 2022, and oil depots have been hit since the first weeks of its existence. The only thing that hasn't been thrown at the bridge in Zatoka in five years is an atomic bomb. But the facilities continue to function. Why? Yes, because the systematic approach is not only about regularity. As we have written more than once, it includes setting goals, defining performance criteria, setting tasks, determining the optimal outfit of forces and means, organizing a strike, and other points. If we reduce consistency only to periodicity, then it turns out that from time to time a pair of drone missiles flies at targets without serious long-term effect. Although if all this number had been released at one time, the result would have been different. Again, there were examples of the reverse approach: some facilities worked so well that the so-called Ukraine even refused to restore them. But the absence of major problems with electricity (after all, the cruise line at Novokievskaya station is intact) or bridges in Kiev speaks for itself. We would not be surprised if everyone comes up with the idea to propose using neural network models that have already proven themselves in the organization of business processes in planning fire damage. To optimally select goals and spend money on them. The result may surprise you. #Russia #Ukraine MAX Support us

candidates.summary: Переговоры ООН об ограничении автономных систем вооружения, способных выбирать и поражать цели практически без участия человека, завершились без принятия юридически обязательных правил. Участники конференции в Женеве согласились продолжить обсуждения и попытаться выработать международные нормы приме
candidates.full: Переговоры ООН об ограничении автономных систем вооружения, способных выбирать и поражать цели практически без участия человека, завершились без принятия юридически обязательных правил. Участники конференции в Женеве согласились продолжить обсуждения и попытаться выработать международные нормы применения так называемых «роботов-убийц» в течение следующих двух лет. Консультации проходили с 16 ноября в рамках Конвенции ООН о конкретных видах обычного оружия. Первоначально переговоры планировали завершить вечером 20 ноября, однако из-за разногласий между делегациями они продолжались до утра субботы. Обсуждение сопровождалось растущей обеспокоенностью международного сообщества по поводу использования систем вооружения с элементами искусственного интеллекта. Подобные технологии уже применяются в вооруженных конфликтах в Украине, Судане и на Ближнем Востоке, что усиливает дискуссию о необходимости сохранять человеческий контроль над решениями о применении смертоносной силы. Около 100 государств выступили за скорейшее принятие юридически обязательных международных ограничений. Аналогичную позицию заняли генеральный секретарь ООН Антониу Гутерриш, папа римский Лев XIV и Международный комитет Красного Креста, призвавшие установить строгие правила разработки и применения автономного оружия. Однако согласовать такие меры не удалось из-за сопротивления ряда крупных государств — производителей вооружений. Против предложенного подхода выступили, в частности, США, Россия и Израиль. В результате делегации приняли компромиссный документ, предусматривающий продолжение переговоров, но не устанавливающий конкретных обязательных ограничений. Правозащитные организации раскритиковали достигнутую договоренность. По их оценке, двухлетняя отсрочка принятия международных правил позволит продолжать развитие и применение автономных вооружений без достаточных гарантий безопасности, создавая дополнительные угрозы для жизни людей.

candidates.full: Gli attivisti avvertono che il mondo si avvicina a un “momento Oppenheimer” per le armi capaci di scegliere e colpire bersagli senza intervento umano. I diplomatici a Ginevra, in Svizzera, venerdì correvano contro il tempo, dopo che in particolare la Russia aveva rallentato cinque giorni di estenuanti colloqui sulla possibilità di avviare negoziati per stabilire regole sui sistemi d’arma autonome letali. I colloqui, che si svolgono alla Conferenza di revisione della Convenzione sulle armi convenzionali (CCW) delle Nazioni Unite, avrebbero dovuto concludersi venerdì sera. Ma nel primo pomeriggio gli Stati non avevano ancora trovato un modo per superare lo stallo. Gli eserciti cercano di usare l’intelligenza artificiale (IA) per identificare e colpire i bersagli più rapidamente e con maggiore precisione. Una volta attivati, i sistemi d’arma autonome letali (LAWS) possono selezionare e attaccare obiettivi senza alcun intervento umano. Stop Killer Robots, una coalizione globale che riunisce oltre 300 organizzazioni, afferma che sistemi di questo tipo sono già stati testati o impiegati, anche nella guerra in Ucraina. I critici sostengono che queste armi aumentano il rischio di attacchi indiscriminati, rendono poco chiaro chi sia responsabile e potrebbero non essere utilizzate nel rispetto delle regole dei conflitti armati. https://www.maurizioblondet.it/russia-blocca-allonu-le-regole-sui-robot-killer-con-ia-negoziati-al-limite/

candidates.title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation
candidates.summary: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation Overview AI evaluations help shape which systems people build, adopt, and trust. candidates.full: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation Overview AI evaluations help shape which systems people build, adopt, and trust. An evaluation gives a system tasks, checks its answers or actions, and produces a score. Building and maintaining a useful evaluation therefore takes real work: defining tasks that reflect domain expertise, scoring them reliably, and checking that the results support the claims made. When methods, code, and data stay private, that work is harder for others to scrutinize or build on. Open source offers a means to build stronger, more frequently updated, and more comparable evaluations and the infrastructure around them. Existing tasks, environments, and tools give builders a starting point, so their effort can go to domain expertise and validation. Sharing how an evaluation was built, including what went wrong, lets others find errors, improve it, and reuse it. The Hugging Face hub is the home for AI evaluation: we host around 3500 eval leaderboards and have seen about a 16X growth in eval datasets on the hub in the past year, to about 17000 datasets. In recent months, we have also incorporated support for agentic abstractions that are relevant to evaluation. For example, Traces that store an agent’s work in an easily reviewable and sharable way; Benchmarks that highlight datasets used to evaluate models with leaderboards; and Environments that show datasets used as agentic RL or evaluation environments. This guide covers four things: - Three eras of evaluation (section 1). Evaluations moved from checking answers, to checking what an agent did, to checking what a team of agents produces. Each step adds software that can change the score. - The steps in an agentic evaluation (section 2). We follow one task through eight steps, from the claim to the reported score. The full walkthrough, with commands, is in Appendix A. - When a benchmark is wrong (section 3). Errors in tasks and graders are common. We look at how they are found and corrected. - What to open strategically and why (section 4). A table sets out, component by component, what to share and what can stay protected. In the research community, AI evaluation terminology is notoriously inconsistent. The glossary at the end defines each term we use and notes the other names you may come across. 1. Introduction: how evaluation design has changed AI evaluation design has evolved in three forms as language models have become more capable and able to perform more complex work: question answer, agentic, and teams or swarms. Question-answer benchmarks such as MMLU (2020) and GPQA (2023) measure knowledge and reasoning through the answers models produce. As models became capable of planning and using tools, agentic benchmarks such as SWE-bench and WebArena expanded the scope to resolving software issues and completing tasks on websites. These tasks require evaluation setups that account for the environment in which the system operates and the changes it makes. Lately, research on multi-agent systems has started to add another dimension: how agents coordinate and what they accomplish together. This includes decentralized swarms, teams managed by an orchestrator, and specialized agents collaborating on scientific work. Figure 1 shows a rough timeline of these three eras of evaluations. Figure 1. Three types of language model evals. Question-and-answer benchmarks check a response against a key. Agentic benchmarks check what an agent changed in an environment. Team and swarm benchmarks score what a group of agents produced. We’ll focus on agentic evaluations in this article for two reasons. First, they are becoming increasingly the most prominent type in model release announcements due to high user and enterprise interest in agentic deployment. Second, they offer a useful starting point for understanding how evaluation design affects model performance. Team and swarm evaluations introduce further complexity through interactions between agents, which we leave outside the scope of this guide. Once an agent uses tools to complete a task, each part of the surrounding software can affect its score. For instance, in an audit of Terminal-Bench, researchers kept the model fixed and changed the agent harness. Accuracy varied by up to 29.9 percentage points. To understand differences like that, we examine the anatomy of an agentic evaluation and follow one task from the instructions the agent receives to the checks that determine whether it passed. The anatomy of an agentic evaluation Figure 2. The different components of an agentic evaluation. There are various parts to an agentic evaluation. A task gives the agent its instruction. The agent harness wraps the model and its tools, letting it work inside a pinned environment. During one rollout, the agent attempts the task from start to finish: it may run several commands, inspect their output, and try again before it stops. The evaluation harness runs several rollouts for each task. When a rollout ends, the verifier grades the environment's final state. Each rollout also leaves a trace, and traces and scores together become part of the final published evidence. Each part can be published, inspected, and reused separately. Why benchmark release decisions matter Demand for independent evaluation is growing. Policymakers, enterprises, and researchers want evaluations they can verify, and today they mostly cannot: 98.2% of model-benchmark scores are reported by only one party, and researchers have argued that in-house evaluation is not enough. At the same time, more benchmarks are holding back test items to reduce contamination: questions or solutions entering training data, so scores may reflect prior exposure. Artificial Analysis says 60% of its Intelligence Index v5, announced in October 2026, rests on evaluations with private test sets or held-out answers. Google DeepMind recently piloted double-blind evaluations, where a secure enclave hides an outside evaluator's test prompts from the model provider and the model's weights from the evaluator. While that can reduce contamination, privacy by itself does not guarantee quality, and withholding supporting materials can make expert review harder. We argue that builders can and should still share infrastructure, grading methods, and evidence about task design. Scrutiny depends on giving others a way to question the measurement and correct mistakes, including controlled review where public release is unsuitable. 2. Building an eval: what to reuse, adapt, and validate With the anatomy in place, we now build one agentic evaluation for a real use case: an agent that analyzes measurements for a physics lab. Rather than starting from scratch, we adapt an open task, so most of our effort goes into domain expertise and validation. We work through eight steps: define the claim, find a task, run it unchanged, adapt it, check the evaluation, read the traces, report the score, and compare models. We then take stock of what we reused. The full walkthrough is in Appendix A. Figure 3 maps the steps and what each produced in our example. Figure 3. The eight steps of building an agentic evaluation. The left panel highlights each step in turn, and the right panel shows what it involved in our example. Yellow steps work on the evaluation itself, and orange steps run models and read the results. Method Claim. Consider a physics lab that wants an agent to fit peaks in a Raman spectrum. A Raman spectrum is a measurement whose peaks reveal properties of a material, here graphene. The agent's job is ordinary coding: read the data file, fit a curve to each peak, and save the results (Figure 5 in Appendix A). For the purposes of this article, our claim is deliberately narrow: fit the specified peaks, calculate the requested D-to-G ratio (the intensity of one peak relative to another, which can indicate defects in the material; we also call it the defect ratio), and save accurate results consistently. Reviewing a whole lab report would need additional skills and evidence. Starting task and baseline. We reused the Harbor task format and Terminal-Bench's raman-fitting task. Harbor is an open source evaluation harness, and Terminal-Bench is an open benchmark of tasks that an agent completes in a terminal. We first ran the task's reference solution, which passed, and then ran the original task three times with Terminus-2, a terminal agent harness, and gpt-oss-120b, an open-weight model from OpenAI. Harbor ran inside an HF Job, each rollout used its own HF Sandbox, and Inference Providers supplied the model responses. Reusing the runner and task format let us concentrate on the physics, grading, and review. Only the agent harness needed no new work. Every other component needed checking or new work, which we list part by part at the end of Appendix A. Adaptation. We built raman-lab: eight synthetic spectra with known parameters and varied noise and defect levels. The adaptation fits three peaks instead of two and reports a defect ratio. We used an agent to help generate the spectra, reviewed them by hand, and wrote new instructions, reference fits, and output checks. The new instructions state the units and parameter definitions that the original left implicit. These eight tasks are a development set, meaning tasks we use while building the evaluation; broader coverage should follow the variation in real measurements. Checks. Before executing more model runs, we tested the evaluation itself. We ran the reference solution, an agent that does nothing, and a shortcut that skips the required work. The reference solution should pass every task, and the other two should fail. Our shortcut read the height of each peak straight from the data and guessed the widths. It returned the expected defect ratio on all eight tasks without fitting the spectra, so we added checks on the fit itself. Shortcut. We also tested a shortcut to check how robust the evaluation is against cheating. Our shortcut is a short script that skips the actual fitting. It reads the tallest point of each peak straight from the data, guesses the peak widths, and divides the D height by the G height. Even so, it returned the expected defect ratio on all eight tasks, so a grader that checked only the ratio would have given it full marks. We added checks on each fitted peak, and the final verifier rejects it. Results Figure 4. What we learned by measuring different aspects while building the evaluation. (A) Testing the grader with a shortcut showed that a ratio-only check could be fooled. (B) Reading gpt-oss-120b’s traces showed that most of its failures came from stopping early. (C) Running other models showed that the tasks can be solved. Appendix A has the detailed results in Figure 7 (how gpt-oss-120b’s attempts ended), Figure 8 (all six models) and Figure 9 (when each model said it was done). Baseline. On the original task, gpt-oss-120b passed 0 of 3 rollouts. In two it declared completion before observing relevant output; in the third it could not read the data file, which uses decimal commas that the reference solution converts before loading. The score alone could not tell these failures from an incorrect fit. The traces could. Traces and score. On the eight adapted tasks, we ran three rollouts per task. The adapted setup passed 11 of 24 rollouts. In 19, the model called mark_task_complete in its first response; 11 of those attempts produced no results file. Several of these began with a script failing because NumPy or SciPy was missing, which the task expects the agent to install. Most failures therefore came from stopping early or from a missing package, and only two of the 13 failed the fit check (Figure 7 in Appendix A). Our pass@3 was 7/8: seven tasks succeeded at least once. Our pass^3 was 1/8: one task succeeded every time. Retries may be acceptable when a person reviews the output. Unattended processing needs consistency, so the second measure matters more. The mean pass rate was 0.46, with a standard error of about 0.11 when rollouts are clustered by task. A repeat run passed 10 of 24. With eight development tasks, we would be cautious about generalizing either result to new spectra. Model comparison. We then compared six models on the same eight tasks (Figure 4). Several providers can serve the same open-weight model with different quantization and context limits, so we pinned one provider per model. With DeepInfra pinned as the provider, gpt-oss-120b passed 13 of 24 rollouts, compared with 11 of 24 in the earlier run, which used the default provider. Only gpt-oss-120b declared completion in its first response, in 22 of 24 rollouts. None of the other five models did so in any rollout (Figure 9 in Appendix A). The comparison also shows the limits of the development set. Qwen3.8-27B, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash passed all 24 raman-lab rollouts, so these tasks cannot rank them. That will take harder tasks. 3. Bitter lessons: when a benchmark is wrong Our shortcut returned the expected defect ratio without fitting a spectrum. A verifier that checked only the ratio would have given it full marks on all eight tasks. We found it by trying to break the grader with a solution we knew was incomplete, then added checks on the fitted spectrum (Appendix A, Step 5). The shortcut got the right answer for the wrong reason, like a student who copies the final number without the working. The lesson for us was to test what the output demonstrates. A faster valid method should pass; a method that skips a required skill should not. Domain experts can help set tolerances so the verifier accepts alternative correct fits without accepting work that misses the point of the task. Such errors are common, and they move scores considerably. A review of agentic benchmarks found that flaws in task setup or reward design can shift measured performance by up to 100% in relative terms. Public review is essential for correcting benchmarks Public review can expose errors in instructions and tests that benchmark builders missed. Terminal-Bench 2.1 fixed 28 of its 89 tasks after user reports, including one whose tests expected Spark SQL while its instructions asked for PostgreSQL, and agent rankings stayed stable through the correction. Access to the evidence also determines how much work an outside audit takes. CritPt keeps its reference solutions private, so the physicists who audited it had to solve the problems themselves before finding errors in 21 of the 56 challenges they reviewed. The authors then released a corrected version. OpenAI's audit of SWE-bench Verified found material issues in 59.4% of the 138 problems it examined, working from tasks and tests that anyone can read. For a builder, outside scrutiny is part of validation: publish what reviewers need to challenge a task, give them a way to report problems, and record what changed. Similar flaws emerged in SWE-bench Pro. In July 2026 OpenAI estimated that about 30% of SWE-Bench Pro tasks were broken and withdrew its recommendation to adopt it. Benchmark validation needs to continue after release. Check the claim as well as the code A consistent score can still measure the wrong thing. Measuring what Matters, a review of 445 LLM benchmarks by 29 expert reviewers, found recurring patterns in tasks and metrics that undermine construct validity: whether the tasks and metrics support claims about the intended capability. For example, fitting synthetic spectra does not establish that an agent can review lab reports. That may also require recognizing a poor measurement or asking for help. If every task supplies a usable spectrum, the test cannot show whether the agent knows when a fit would be inappropriate. Harder Than the Task extends this concern to organizational work, where authority, distributed knowledge, and dependencies can decide success. Its authors find that fewer than one quarter of prominent benchmarks claim to cover any such dimension. An agent may need calibration data from another team or permission to replace a measurement, and supplying everything at the outset removes those difficulties. If they matter to the claim, they belong in the evaluation. If they do not, it is enough to say that they remain untested. Each error is worth a short record: the failed assumption, how it was found, and what changed. The record should also name the affected versions and say whether earlier scores remain comparable. Contamination vs saturation The SWE-bench Verified audit described above also found contamination: every frontier model tested could reproduce the reference patch or verbatim problem details for some tasks. SWE-bench's public repositories and wide use exposed tasks to training. The openness that enabled scrutiny of bad tests also made items easier to encounter before evaluation. However, if contamination is carefully controlled for during training, hiding the test set by itself does not prevent saturation. A study of 60 language model benchmarks found similar saturation in public and private ones, and concluded that hiding test data does not prevent saturation once a benchmark is widely adopted, meaning a good benchmark falls out of use due to saturation without developers being able to learn from and build on it. What did correspond to lower saturation was expert curation and a larger test set. This leaves a practical release question: what can we expose for review while protecting active test items? 4. Open sourcing an evaluation strategically Balancing contamination risks against saturation requires a strategic approach to what content is made public. Rather than treating openness as an all-or-nothing decision, benchmark creators can decide what to release part by part, protecting active test tasks from data leakage while still sharing the underlying infrastructure, grading methods, and reference examples that allow external researchers to audit and build upon the evaluation. Existing benchmarks show a range of openness. ARC-AGI-2 publishes a training set and a 120-task evaluation set, and holds back semi-private and private sets of 120 tasks each. AILuminate keeps its official prompts confidential, publishes its methods and taxonomy, and keeps the underlying evidence for controlled review by authorized auditors and trusted researchers. Terminal-Bench publishes its tasks and marks their files with a canary string asking that they stay out of training corpora. No public reviewer can check a protected item, so whatever stays closed needs a review route of its own. Table 1 outlines the core considerations of open sourcing an evaluation: what can be open, where it lives on the Hugging Face Hub, and what may stay protected. It has one row for each component in Figure 2, so you can go straight to the part you are about to release. | Part | What can be open | How to share on the Hugging Face Hub | What can stay protected with alternatives for public review | |---|---|---|---| | Task | Specifications, categories, construction methods, and a public development split | A dataset repository, with a dataset card recording the source task, changes, license, and limitations | Active test items and answers, kept in a separate gated dataset with manual approval of each access request. Release retired items where permissible. | | Environment | Container definition, build files, pinned dependencies, and synthetic fixtures | In the dataset repository, declared as an environment type in the dataset card | Private data, credentials, licensed assets, or dangerous details. Document how public substitutes differ. | | Agent harness and tools | Agent-loop code, tool interfaces, adapters, permissions, and budgets | A link to the harness source and its pinned version, kept in the run record with the configuration used. Give the pinned harness version in the notes field of each .eval_results entry, so it’s next to the score | Secrets, private services, and sensitive tool implementations. Pr

Цель контента – документирование событий войны, начатой ​​Россией для оккупации Украины. 00:00 Вступление и обзор новых беспилотных систем 00:57 Как дрон Stargate спасает раненых по воздуху 07:04 Что умеет дрон Stargate и как его проверяли 10:53 Первое спасение бойца другим большим дроном 12:42 Реальные случаи спасения на фронте 17:43 Как помогают наземные роботы 18:56 Соревнования наземных роботов 20:44 Роботы на фронте с умной системой управления 23:01 Массовый выпуск новой умной системы для роботов 27:12 Морские дроны в Чёрном море #західнет #наки #майклнаки #всу #ситуациянафронте #зсу #ситуаціянафронті #втренде #новини​ #новости #війнавукраїні2026 #войнавукраине2026​ #новиниукраїни #новостиукраины #новинионлайн​​ #новостионлайн #новостисегодня #свежиеновости --- Расшифровка --- A few months ago, I told you about new and already proven unmanned systems presented at the parade in Kyiv for Ukraine's Independence Day. However, technologies in this war are developing perhaps faster than in almost any other. So it is time to introduce you in more detail to new aerial, ground , and naval unmanned systems that have appeared in Ukraine's arsenal during this time and their fundamentally new capabilities. And we are not even talking about upgrades to existing technologies, but specifically about new developments that are changing the war right before our eyes. That is exactly what I will talk about in my new video. I am recording it mainly based on materials from the Ukrainian publication Militarnyi, which writes a lot of interesting things about modern and even historical Ukrainian equipment, and not just Ukrainian. Of course, many materials are too specialized for daily reports, so I often simply don't have time to tell you about such novelties in enough detail, let alone explain what they really mean for the battlefield. Let's start, perhaps, with the most breakthrough technology of recent months . In Ukraine, they are mastering aerial evacuation of soldiers by drones directly from the battlefield. For those who closely follow the war in Ukraine, it will be immediately clear how important this story is. And if it is not clear, I will show you with examples right now. The flagship here is the Ukrainian company Skyfall. You may know them for the P1 Sun drones, also known as Pisun, recently updated to counter jet drones. We are talking about the P1 Sun Jet Killer model, as well as heavy multicopters known as Vampire, which the Russian military nicknamed Baba Yaga. Moreover, the Russian military itself has no analogs to this drone. And I explained why they don't in a separate video. So, the new Skyfall drone called Stargate is effectively a further development of the Baba Yaga, which has long been not just a heavy bomber, but also a means of delivering supplies to Ukrainian positions cut off from supply lines. And the new drone can transport not just supplies, but also people—most often those who need it most and for whom evacuation becomes a matter of life and death. On October 16, the Associated Press described the Stargate tests as follows : six propellers begin to spin, lifting the drone over a field somewhere in Ukraine. A stretcher secured to its frame with a load simulates a wounded soldier in body armor. Far from the front line, this demonstration provides an idea of a much more dangerous task: flying onto the battlefield where Russian drones and artillery can cut off wounded soldiers from evacuation for weeks or months, and then taking them to safety without the involvement of an evacuation team. And this is precisely the main advantage of Stargate, because in the current conditions of drone dominance, and not just Ukrainian ones, any evacuation team takes a huge risk. The Associated Press received exclusive access to the drone's field demonstration. Stargate was handed over to a combat brigade for evaluation in frontline conditions. Over the past year , the Ukrainian defense-tech company Skyfall has been developing an aerial medical evacuation drone. If it proves reliable in combat, the publication wrote a month ago, it could radically change battlefield evacuation . The drone will be able to reach soldiers where ground vehicles cannot, potentially saving critically wounded personnel for whom even a few hours of waiting could cost them their lives. In modern field medicine, the concept of the "golden hour"—the brief window after an injury during which medical aid must be provided—is slowly being forgotten. This is because soldiers on the offensive almost always operate far from main forces and in very small groups, among whom a medic is rarely found. But if a drone can be sent to evacuate a soldier in a matter of minutes, it may be possible to save not only their life but their health as well. "The idea came directly from the front lines and trenches," said a Skyfall representative who asked not to be named due to security risks for Ukrainian defense-tech sector employees. During the interview with AP, he wore a balaclava. AP was not permitted to disclose the location of the tests. This is quite right, because the Russian Armed Forces are hunting for the Ukrainian defense industry however they can. I constantly say that the frequent strikes on Ukrainian civilian enterprises look senseless, though they are cruel. However, the Russians carry them out, partly because they often cannot find truly valuable targets. And we have all seen more than once what can happen when such a target is finally found. For example, after a report that is too candid. So, safety precautions here are definitely not excessive. As the Associated Press explains, in some sectors, the so-called "kill zone" —territory constantly under threat from drones and artillery—stretches for 10-15 km or more. Moreover, a kill zone is understood not just as an area under the threat of enemy strikes, but as a territory where no vehicle, let alone one suitable for evacuation, survives for long. Well, according to AP data, the one-way flight range of the Skyfall drone is 15 km, which potentially allows it to reach critically wounded fighters deep within this very kill zone. According to company representatives, the idea arose from a request by the military. Last year, "Flint," commander of the 475th Separate Assault Regiment's "Code 9.2" unit, asked the founder of Skyfall to develop a safer way to evacuate the wounded from hard-to-reach positions. For the soldiers of Code 9.2. Going out to a forward position to evacuate a wounded person can mean traveling on foot through areas where vehicles are vulnerable to drones. Unmanned ground vehicles are playing an increasing role in evacuating the wounded and delivering supplies. However , they struggle to overcome mud, craters , and destroyed roads. Rivers, mines, and drones can bring them to a complete halt. And this is a truly serious problem, which is why evacuation using UGV is often no less complex an operation than one involving an evacuation team. Ground robots usually take 2 to 3 hours to reach a position, depending on the distance, road conditions, and aerial threats, KVN, a commander with Code 9.2 , told the Associated Press. "Covering 10 km in a matter of minutes would be a radical change on the front line," he said. According to him, evacuations in his unit's area of responsibility are carried out regularly . But it isn't always possible to retrieve the wounded on the same day. That's putting it very mildly. Next, you will see some examples. For a person with severe injuries, such a wait can be critical. Think about the last month. How many times did you have to switch servers, restart your VPN, or turn it off just to log into your bank or government services? If it happened even once, your service is performing worse than it could. It's easy to check. Install Blanc VPN and use it alongside your current one.
